> Thanks Naomi — this is helpful. A few follow-ups from our security team (copied):

> 1) When a customer selects EU-only processing, can you guarantee that request execution and any transient caches remain within EU-controlled regions (no US hop for routing or cache persistence)?
> 2) Which named subprocessors will have access to request payloads or logs (even transiently)? We need contractual assurances and a list of contracts where Redwood acts as controller/processor.
> 3) Deletion: if we ask for a customer-data purge for a specific workspace, what systems are touched and what is the expected wall-clock time for irreversible deletion (including caches and backups)?
> 4) KMS / key control: do you support bringing our own keys (BYOK) for encryption at rest and for S3 object/material keys?

Thanks — good questions. Short answers (below) plus attached brief with more detail. Marissa/Karthik — adding you to help with the contract/evidence items and to offer tech options.

1) EU-only processing: for our hosted product we support region pinning at the tenant level; if you select EU-only execution we schedule inference on capacity physically located in EU cloud regions (we currently operate in europe-west1 and europe-west4). Request routing may traverse internal load-balancers inside the same cloud region; Redwood does not intentionally route EU-pinned traffic through US infrastructure. Transient in-memory caches (KV cache) are ephemeral and TTL-bound; we consider them non-persistent — they are not written to external long-term storage.

2) Named subprocessors & access scope: the short list (attached CSV) includes core cloud providers (Google Cloud Platform and Microsoft Azure in EU ops), observability (Datadog for metrics — only aggregated traces unless explicit request logging enabled), managed logging bucket (customer logs are stored in region when tenant pinning is used), and our CI/CD vendor for package build artifacts. We do not share raw inference payloads with analytics vendors by default. The attached subprocessor-inventory-brief.csv includes contract role (processor/controller) and the minimal access each subprocessor has.

3) Deletion workflow and expected timings: when you request workspace-level purges we run a coordinated workflow that: (a) invalidate KV caches immediately, (b) delete blobs/objects from regional object stores (S3/GCS) within 24–72 hours, (c) remove index/metadata rows from primary DBs in 72 hours, and (d) purge backups per our backup retention windows — we offer a post-request backup scrub for customers requiring faster irrevocable erasure (subject to the Dedicated/Private options). We will provide a certificate of deletion for audit if needed. Note that immutable infrastructure snapshots may persist for a limited time — we can include a contractual SLA for tighter timelines under Dedicated/Private.

4) KMS/BYOK: we support customer-managed keys via standard KMS integrations (Azure Key Vault, GCP KMS). With BYOK in hosted mode, encryption at rest uses your keys for object storage and the primary DB; some ephemeral in-memory encryption keys are still managed by Redwood for runtime. With Dedicated/Private we can offer broader BYOK coverage and more clear-cut separation of key custody.

Next steps: we can provide SOC 2 Type II report excerpts (redacted), our executed DPA, and the subprocessor SOWs. I uploaded a short evidence pack and signed DPA to the DocuSign link below; if you want wholesale contract language edits we can route through legal.
